attribution.changes: Article numbers and titles are quoted; the criteria are written for this prototype. Only the text published in the Official Journal is authentic.

candidates.name: Gradient-boosted trees with monotonic constraints
candidates.fit: Predicts the probability of default from bureau and account-behaviour features with the accuracy of boosted trees, while monotonic constraints keep each feature's effect in the direction an underwriter expects.

criteria.text: Calibration: predicted default rates match observed rates in each score band on a held-out quarter.
Four-fifths rule on approval rates across the five protected attributes.
Reason codes come from each applicant's own feature contributions, so a declined applicant can contest them.

source.title: GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), Article 22: Automated individual decision-making, including profiling

candidates.gaps: The benchmarks table has no benchmark for tabular credit models: DiscrimEval (s100 #64) tests language models making decisions, not a scoring model.

candidates.name: Points-based logistic scorecard
candidates.fit: A transparent scorecard whose points per attribute underwriters and applicants can read, at some cost in accuracy against the trees.

criteria.text: Discrimination (Gini) within an agreed margin of the current model on the same held-out quarter.
Points per attribute published in the model card.
A plain-language explanation of each decline that an applicant can act on.

source.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 86: Right to explanation of individual decision-making

candidates.gaps: The benchmarks table has no benchmark for tabular credit models: DiscrimEval (s100 #64) tests language models making decisions, not a scoring model.

criterion.text: The role charter names who confirms each decline and may overrule the score.

criterion.text: Four-fifths rule on approvals across protected attributes, re-run after each re-weighting.

criterion.text: Reason codes tested against score contributions on a sample of declines.

candidates.name: Hosted large language model with retrieval and citation checks
candidates.fit: Answers service agents' questions from the indexed policy library, with each answer tied to the passage it cites.

criteria.text: Citation-support rate on sampled answers, against the pilot baseline.

candidates.gaps: The benchmarks table has no benchmark built on a bank's own policy library; the groundedness evaluation stands in for one.

candidates.name: Smaller self-hosted model with the same retrieval
candidates.fit: Keeps customer text inside the bank, at the cost of weaker reasoning on long or unusual policy questions.

criteria.text: The same citation-support evaluation as the hosted model, run before switching.

candidates.gaps: The benchmarks table has no benchmark built on a bank's own policy library; the groundedness evaluation stands in for one.

criterion.text: A nightly check that every indexed policy is the current version.
Citation-support rate on sampled answers, reviewed weekly.
The provider contract states zero retention of prompts, checked in the supplier assessment.

candidates.name: Embedding similarity ranking with protected attributes masked
candidates.fit: Ranks each application against the requisition by text similarity, after names, addresses and graduation years are masked.

criteria.text: Selection-rate ratio by group on held-out requisitions, within the four-fifths rule, in the independent bias audit.
Training and reference data examined for bias before each version.

source.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 10: Data and data governance

candidates.gaps: The benchmarks table has no G or X benchmark for ranking CVs against a requisition; the bias audit and recruiter review stand in for one.

candidates.name: Rules-based screening on stated requirements, ranked by recruiters
candidates.fit: Screens only on requirements the requisition states, such as the right to work and certifications, and leaves the ranking to recruiters.

criteria.text: Selection-rate ratio by group on held-out requisitions, within the four-fifths rule, in the independent bias audit.
Each rejected candidate can be told which stated requirement was not met.
